Credits.title: Credits
Credits.intro: Renshi builds on the official HSK 3.0 syllabus and on open projects that allow their work to be used with attribution. Renshi's own sentences and notes add to these sources; content derived from Gushi is shared under the same license.
Credits.syllabusWho: Chinese Test International (中文考试服务网), official syllabus published in November 2025
Credits.gushi: Spanish meanings and some of the examples
Credits.gushiWho: Gushi, HSK 3.0 word lists translated by hand
Credits.makemeahanzi: Which parts each character is made of

Lab.title: Lab
Lab.intro: This is where we try ideas before they reach Renshi. Some are still being tested; others are already part of the app and stay here to tell how they got there.
Lab.bannerTesting: Pilot being tested, not the final version
Lab.ideasTitle: What would you like us to try?
Lab.ideasText: If you teach or learn Chinese and have an idea that would help in class, tell us. The best ideas start here.
Lab.unavailable: The demo isn't available right now.
Lab.tryPandaHint: Type a made-up six-letter code: the panda follows the active box and reacts if the class doesn't exist.

votingSteps.2026-10-11: Anonymous voting: students join with a code in a text field, no account needed.
votingSteps.2026-10-12a: Voting follows the card the teacher is showing, and the code stays visible to the class.
votingSteps.2026-10-12b: The code becomes six boxes: a missing letter is obvious right away.
votingSteps.2026-10-12c: The panda arrives: it watches the active box and reacts if the code doesn't exist.
votingSteps.2026-10-12d: After fixing a letter, the cursor moves on by itself.
votingSteps.2026-10-16: If the phone loses its connection, it says so.

escritura.title: Writing
escritura.summary: Students trace the character with a finger: tracing or from memory, with three tolerance levels.

gramatica.title: Grammar
gramatica.summary: Build sentences with 12 HSK 1 grammar points, with a mode to project in class.

tinta.title: Chinese ink
tinta.summary: The character is drawn with brush edges, bleeding ink and rice paper.
tinta.body: In class, the “Ink” button (or the I key) switches the plain stroke to Chinese ink. Here are both, side by side.

votacion.title: Students vote
votacion.summary: Anonymous voting from the phone, with the panda that guides the code.
votacion.body: It started as a text field and grew with every test class. This is how it became what students use today.

frases.title: Sentences in another language
frases.summary: Back-of-card sentences start in Chinese, Spanish or English: the class tries to say them in Chinese, then reveal.
frases.body: On the back of the card, the presentation bar has a selector “Sentences in: 中文 · ES · EN” (key L). In Chinese you reveal the Spanish and English translation; in Spanish or English the class tries to say the sentence in Chinese and reveals it with the 中 button, with pinyin as a hint.

Lab.frasesStep1: Open the sample class and flip the card (Space).
Lab.frasesStep2: In the bottom bar, pick “ES” or “EN” under “Sentences in” (or press L).
Lab.frasesStep3: Each sentence shows 🔊, 中 and pinyin: listen, try to say it in Chinese, then reveal with 中.
Lab.tryInDemo: Try it in the sample class
